docs.title: OpenClaw Observability
docs.text: OpenTelemetry observability for OpenClaw AI agents — traces, metrics, and logs.

docs.title: Two Approaches
docs.text: This documentation covers two complementary approaches to OpenClaw observability:

docs.title: 1. Official Diagnostics Plugin (Built-in)
docs.text:
OpenClaw v2026.2+ includes built-in OTel support via diagnostics.otel config. Best for:

  • ✅ Operational metrics (tokens, costs, durations)
  • ✅ Gateway health monitoring
  • ✅ Log forwarding
  • ✅ Simple setup (config only)

docs.title: 2. Custom Hook-Based Plugin (This Repo)
docs.text:
A plugin that hooks into the agent lifecycle for deeper tracing. Best for:

  • ✅ Connected distributed traces
  • ✅ Per-tool-call spans
  • ✅ Request lifecycle visibility
  • ✅ Debugging agent behavior

Don't run both at once — both initialize the OTel SDK and can conflict (global tracer/meter provider state, see Limitations). Pick one; the two quick starts below are alternatives, not steps to combine.

docs.title: Option A: This plugin (otel-observability)
docs.text:
1. Clone the repo at a release tag and build it (npm ci && npm run build)
  2. Add it to plugins.load.paths
  3. Configure it in plugins.entries.otel-observability (including hooks.allowConversationAccess: true)
  4. Clear the jiti cache and restart the gateway

See Getting Started for detailed instructions.

docs.title: Option B: Official plugin instead (5 minutes, config only)
docs.text:
If you only need what the official plugin covers, add this to ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json instead — and don't also enable this plugin:

{
  "diagnostics": {
    "enabled": true,
    "otel": {
      "enabled": true,
      "endpoint": "https://otlp-collector.example.com",
      "serviceName": "openclaw-gateway",
      "traces": true,
      "metrics": true,
      "logs": true
    }
  }
}

Then restart:

openclaw gateway restart

docs.text: How OpenClaw observability works — both the official plugin and custom hook-based approach.

docs.title: Plugin Lifecycle
docs.text:
OpenClaw drives plugins through three phases. Mixing them up is the single most common way to break the custom plugin — if typed hooks are registered in the wrong phase, the gateway never sees them and no spans are produced. The current layout:

┌──────────────┐      ┌──────────────┐      ┌──────────────┐
│  register()  │ ───▶ │    start()   │ ───▶ │    stop()    │
│  synchronous │      │     async    │      │     async    │
└──────────────┘      └──────────────┘      └──────────────┘
        │                     │                     │
        │                     │                     │
        ▼                     ▼                     ▼
  - initTelemetry()     - initOpenLLMetry()  - stopHooks()
  - api.on(*)           - env bridge         - unsubscribe()
  - api.registerHook()                       - telemetry.flush()
  - api.registerGate…
  - api.on("gateway_stop")
  - api.registerCli()
  - api.registerService()
  - api.registerTool()
        │                     │
        └─── lazy getter ─────┘
           () => telemetry
Phase Runs Responsibility register() Synchronous, before the gateway accepts traffic Build or reuse the OTel runtime (initTelemetry → TracerProvider + MeterProvider), wire every typed hook (message_received, session_start, session_end, before_model_resolve, before_prompt_build, llm_input, llm_output, model_call_started, model_call_ended, before_dispatch, reply_dispatch, before_tool_call, after_tool_call, tool_approval_resolution, tool_result_persist, message_sent, before_agent_finalize, agent_end, before_reset, cron hooks, subagent hooks), event-stream hooks (command:*, gateway:startup), diagnostics listener, RPC method, CLI command, background service, and agent tool. start() Async, once the gateway is ready Perform gateway-only setup: publish content-capture env vars for subprocesses, warn on preload/config mismatches, and optionally wrap LLM SDKs with OpenLLMetry when traces is on. stop() Async, on gateway reload or shutdown Clear the stale-session sweeper setInterval (see b668a4f, ISI-522), unsubscribe from diagnostics, shut down the log pipeline, and call telemetry.flush() so batched spans/metrics drain without destroying providers. gateway_stop Final gateway lifecycle hook Calls telemetry.shutdown() for destructive provider teardown, clears the metric heartbeat interval and preExit symbol, and releases the module-level runtime guard for a real process restart.

docs.title: Lazy telemetry getter
docs.text:
Hooks are registered in register() and resolve the current runtime with a lazy telemetry getter instead of closing over a stale concrete runtime:

let telemetry: TelemetryRuntime | null = null;

// Registered in register(), resolves telemetry at call time.
let stopHooks: (() => void) | null = null;
let unsubscribeDiagnostics: (() => void) | null = null;

telemetry = initTelemetry(config, logger);         // populated in register()
stopHooks = registerHooks(api, () => telemetry, config);
registerDiagnosticsListener(telemetry, logger).then((unsub) => {
  unsubscribeDiagnostics = unsub;
});
api.on("gateway_stop", async () => {
  await telemetry?.shutdown();                     // destructive finalizer
  telemetry = null;
});

api.registerService({
  id: "otel-observability",
  start: async () => {
    if (config.traces) await initOpenLLMetry(config, logger);
  },
  stop: async () => {
    stopHooks?.();                                  // clearInterval
    unsubscribeDiagnostics?.();
    await telemetry?.flush();                       // non-destructive
  },
});

Each hook handler opens with:

const telemetry = getTelemetry();
if (!telemetry) return;

so hook handlers read whichever live runtime register() installed.

docs.title: Hot reload vs. final shutdown
docs.text:
OpenClaw uses the same service stop() callback for config hot-reload and ordinary gateway teardown, and the service context does not provide a reliable "final process exit" discriminator. This plugin therefore treats stop() as a hot-reload-safe drain, not a destructive provider shutdown.

initTelemetry() is idempotent. During hot reload, the new register() call reuses the existing runtime rather than registering a second global TracerProvider or duplicating the metric heartbeat interval. This prevents silent telemetry loss after reload, but it also means trace/metric provider config changes do not take effect until the process restarts. Restart the gateway after changing endpoint, headers, protocol, service name, traces, metrics, sample rate, metrics interval, resource attributes, or preload-backed content capture. The metric heartbeat interval is unref'ed so it does not pin process exit; gateway_stop still performs explicit destructive shutdown when the host emits final gateway teardown.

The runtime still exposes shutdown() for explicit destructive teardown in tests and gateway_stop. During normal operation, forced-exit callers should use globalThis[Symbol.for("openclaw.otel.preExit")] to flush before process.exit(); the plugin sets that symbol during telemetry initialization and clears it from shutdown().

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The custom plugin uses typed plugin hooks — direct callbacks into the agent lifecycle.

Gateway Agent Loop              Custom Plugin
     │                               │
     │  on("message_received")       │
     │ ─────────────────────────────>│  ──> create ROOT span
     │                               │      store in sessionContextMap
     │                               │
     │  on("before_model_resolve")   │
     │ ─────────────────────────────>│  ──> create AGENT TURN span
     │                               │      (child of root)
     │                               │
     │  on("before_prompt_build")    │
     │ ─────────────────────────────>│  ──> enrich AGENT TURN span
     │                               │      with prompt.chars +
     │                               │      session.message_count
     │                               │
     │  on("model_call_started")     │
     │ ─────────────────────────────>│  ──> create CHAT span (per real call)
     │  (once per real LLM call)     │      (child of agent turn)
     │                               │
     │  on("model_call_ended")       │
     │ ─────────────────────────────>│  ──> close CHAT span (no usage here —
     │                               │      this event carries none, see
     │                               │      Data Flow Comparison below)
     │                               │      update llm.requests/.duration
     │                               │      (per-call metrics, 0.11.0+)
     │                               │
     │  on("before_tool_call")       │
     │ ─────────────────────────────>│  ──> open "execute_tool {name}" span
     │  (once per tool call)         │      (child of agent turn)
     │                               │
     │  on("after_tool_call")        │
     │ ─────────────────────────────>│  ──> close tool span, record
     │                               │      openclaw.tool.calls/.duration
     │                               │      (tool_result_persist enriches the
     │                               │      span, or creates + ends one itself
     │                               │      if before_tool_call never fired)
     │                               │
     │  on("agent_end")              │
     │ ─────────────────────────────>│  ──> end agent turn span
     │                               │      end root span
     │                               │      enrich turn span with token
     │                               │      usage (span attributes only —
     │                               │      no token metrics recorded here)

Token and cost metrics don't come from these hooks at all — they come from OpenClaw's diagnostic-event stream, see Data Flow Comparison below.

docs.title: Trace Context Propagation
docs.text:
The key difference is trace context propagation. The custom plugin maintains a session-to-context map:

interface SessionTraceContext {
  rootSpan: Span;           // openclaw.request
  rootContext: Context;     // OTel context with root span
  agentSpan?: Span;         // openclaw.agent.turn
  agentContext?: Context;   // OTel context with agent span
  startTime: number;
}

const sessionContextMap = new Map<string, SessionTraceContext>();

When creating child spans, it uses the stored context:

// Tool span becomes child of agent turn
const span = tracer.startSpan(
  spanNameExecuteTool(toolName),   // "execute_tool <toolName>"
  { kind: SpanKind.INTERNAL },
  sessionCtx.agentContext  // <-- parent context
);

docs.title: Official Plugin: Token Tracking
docs.text:
1. Agent calls LLM via pi-ai
2. pi-ai returns response with .usage
3. Gateway calculates cost
4. Gateway emits "model.usage" event with:
   - usage: {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite}
   - costUsd: 0.0234
   - model: "claude-..."
   - durationMs: 2341
5. diagnostics-otel receives event
6. Creates metrics + span
7. Batches and exports via OTLP

docs.title: Custom Plugin: Token Tracking
docs.text:
0.11.0+ — three separate sources, split by what's exclusively available on each. Request count and duration come from the per-call hook pair; per-call token counts come from per-call diagnostic events (a different mechanism — the hook pair itself carries no usage data); cost is still turn-level only, because no per-call cost field exists anywhere in OpenClaw's plugin API.

Per real model call, via hooks (openclaw.llm.requests / .errors / .duration,
gen_ai.client.operation.duration):
1. Agent calls LLM via pi-ai
2. Gateway fires model_call_started → plugin opens a "chat {model}" span,
   stashes provider/agentId on the session's active context
3. Gateway fires model_call_ended with sanitized call metadata only: timing,
   outcome, provider/model, bounded request-id hashes — no usage field
4. Plugin closes the span and records request-count/error/duration metrics

Per real model call, via diagnostic events (openclaw.llm.tokens.*,
gen_ai.client.token.usage) — requires OpenClaw v2026.9.8+:
1. Gateway emits a "model.call.completed" (or "model.call.error") diagnostic
   event for the call, carrying that call's own usage
   (input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite/total)
2. Plugin records the token counters/histogram once per call. Core guards
   this emission per call itself, so no plugin-side dedup is needed here

Per agent turn, via diagnostic events (openclaw.llm.cost.usd only):
1. Gateway fires the "model.usage" diagnostic event once per turn (summing
   however many real calls happened in it) — the only place cost appears
2. Plugin dedup-checks it against openclaw/openclaw#166289 (a duplicate
   dispatch of this event) and records cost if new

Span enrichment only (no metrics):
- agent_end carries the turn's messages; the plugin uses usage from the
  turn's model.usage event (or, failing that, the messages' own .usage) to
  set gen_ai.usage.* attributes on the openclaw.agent.turn span

Before 0.11.0, tokens were recorded once per turn from model.usage, with an agent_end fallback that used a different, disjoint label schema (no gen_ai.conversation.id). That fallback was removed once tokens moved to the per-call diagnostic events — see docs/telemetry/metrics.md and CHANGELOG.md for the full before/after.

docs.title: Removed attributes — dual-emit window closed (schema 1.3.0)
docs.text:
Schema 1.3.0 (ISI-1004) closes the dual-emit window opened in 1.2.0 (ISI-994). The legacy OTel semconv keys are no longer emitted — dashboards, alerts, and queries must read the stable replacements.

Removed (1.3.0) Stable replacement (shipped in 1.2.0) gen_ai.system gen_ai.provider.name code.function + code.namespace code.function.name (= ${namespace}.${function}) + code.file.path gen_ai.usage.cache_read_tokens gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens gen_ai.usage.cache_write_tokens gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens gen_ai.usage.total_tokens (none — compute input + output)

The constants that exported the removed keys (GEN_AI_SYSTEM, CODE_FUNCTION, CODE_NAMESPACE, GEN_AI_USAGE_CACHE_READ_TOKENS, GEN_AI_USAGE_CACHE_WRITE_TOKENS, GEN_AI_USAGE_TOTAL_TOKENS) are also removed from src/semconv.ts.

Consumer action required:

  • Switch Dynatrace dashboards / DQL queries from gen_ai.system to gen_ai.provider.name.
  • Replace any filter on code.function / code.namespace with code.function.name (combined form) or code.file.path.
  • Update cache-token panels to gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens / gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens.
  • Compute totals as gen_ai.usage.input_tokens + gen_ai.usage.output_tokens — gen_ai.usage.total_tokens is gone.

The resource attribute openclaw.schema.version carried 1.3.0 on every signal from this cut-over onward, so consumers can gate queries on it.

docs.title: Resource identity (ISI-995)
docs.text:
The trace, metric, and log Resources all carry:

  • service.version resolved at module load from openclaw.plugin.json's version field — the legacy hard-coded "0.1.0" placeholder is gone, so version-comparison dashboards now see real plugin releases.
  • An OTel semconv schema_url (currently https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.43.0, pinned to the installed @opentelemetry/semantic-conventions version — tests/version.test.ts fails if the two drift apart) so backends can resolve attribute names against the right registry generation.
  • openclaw.schema.version — the plugin's own attribute-schema version (see Current schema version).

docs.title: Log-attribute hygiene (ISI-995)
docs.text:
Bridged log records emit OTel-stable code.function.name, code.file.path, and code.line.number for the emit site, replacing the older openclaw.log.function, openclaw.log.file, and openclaw.log.line triplet (which duplicated the same semantics in a non-portable namespace and confused log-pipeline filters keyed on code.*).

The pipeline no longer emits openclaw.log.trace_id, openclaw.log.span_id, or openclaw.log.trace_flags either — those fields are already on the OTLP LogRecord itself when the active context is passed to emit(), so the duplicate attribute lines were silent double-records.

docs.title: Batching
docs.text: This plugin uses batched export: - Traces: BatchSpanProcessor (OTel SDK defaults: 5s or 512 spans) - Metrics: PeriodicExportingMetricReader, every metricsIntervalMs (default 30s) - Logs: BatchLogRecordProcessor (5s, up to 512 records per batch)

docs.title: Overhead
docs.text:
Plugin Overhead Source Official Event subscription, metric/span creation Custom Hook interception, context map management

Both are lightweight — the OTel SDK handles batching efficiently.

docs.title: Sampling
docs.text:
Reduce trace volume with sampleRate in this plugin's config — 0.1 keeps 10% of traces:

{
  "plugins": {
    "entries": {
      "otel-observability": {
        "config": {
          "sampleRate": 0.1
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

See Configuration → Trace Sampling for the exact semantics.

docs.title: When to Use Each
docs.text:
Use Case Better fit Minimal setup, config only, no install Official Forwarding all gateway logs Official Per-call token metrics, per-conversation cost/token dashboards Custom Gateway health (queues, sessions, event loop, memory) Either — both emit these Debugging specific requests Custom Understanding agent behavior Custom Tool execution analysis Custom

Don't run both at once. Both plugins initialize their own OTel SDK instance against the same process — running them together risks double-registered global providers and duplicate/conflicting export, not "complete observability." Pick one; see docs/limitations.md and docs/index.md for the full reasoning.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Configure the custom hook-based OTel observability plugin via ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.

docs.title: Full Configuration Example
docs.text:
{
  "plugins": {
    "load": { "paths": ["~/.openclaw/plugins/otel-observability"] },
    "entries": {
      "otel-observability": {
        "enabled": true,
        "hooks": { "allowConversationAccess": true },
        "config": {
          "endpoint": "https://otlp-collector.example.com",
          "protocol": "http",
          "headers": {
            "Authorization": "Bearer ${OTEL_API_KEY}"
          },
          "serviceName": "openclaw-gateway",
          "traces": true,
          "metrics": true,
          "logs": true,
          "sampleRate": 1.0,
          "metricsIntervalMs": 30000
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: plugins.entries.otel-observability.hooks.allowConversationAccess
docs.text: Required, boolean, defaults to unset/false. Sits next to config, not inside it — a sibling field on the plugin entry (see example above). Required on OpenClaw ≥ 2026.4.23 for a path-loaded (non-bundled) plugin to receive conversation-scoped typed-hook events at all (before_model_resolve, llm_input/llm_output, agent_end, and the rest). Without it, those hook registrations are silently dropped — the plugin still logs its "registered" banners, but the handlers never fire, so no openclaw.agent.turn/model-call spans or per-call token metrics reach your backend, with no error logged anywhere. This only gates that these events reach the plugin, not conversation content — content capture is the separate captureContent option below, off by default. See Getting Started for the full explanation and Hooks register but never fire if spans aren't showing up.

docs.title: plugins.entries.otel-observability.config
docs.text:
Plugin entry configuration.

Option Type Default Description endpoint string "http://localhost:4318" OTLP endpoint URL protocol string "http" Protocol: "http" or "grpc" headers object {} Custom HTTP headers (e.g., auth tokens) serviceName string "openclaw-gateway" OTel service name attribute traces boolean true Enable trace export metrics boolean true Enable metrics export logs boolean true Enable log forwarding sampleRate number — Trace sampling rate, 0.0–1.0. Omit to use the SDK default (parentbased_always_on). Overrides OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER / OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG — see Trace Sampling for precedence rules. metricsIntervalMs number 30000 Metrics export interval in milliseconds (values below 1000 are ignored and the default is used) captureContent boolean | object false Span content capture policy resourceAttributes object {} Extra OpenTelemetry resource attributes logConfig object — Filtering rules for which log lines the OTLP log pipeline exports — see Log Filtering (logConfig) signalEndpoints object — Per-signal OTLP endpoint overrides (metrics/logs/traces); falls back to endpoint signalHeaders object — Per-signal header overrides (metrics/logs/traces); replaces headers entirely for that signal collapseEphemeralSessions boolean false Collapse ephemeral per-run session keys (recurring cron jobs, internal-session-effect turns) to a stable job-level identifier on metric labels only — see Metrics Reference for which metrics this affects and Limitations for why it exists enableByModelMetrics boolean false Add a _by_model sibling for every per-conversation LLM metric, with gen_ai.conversation.id/gen_ai.agent.id dropped so it stays rate-able even for a one-shot session — see Metrics Reference for the full list and Limitations for the problem it fixes. Cost note: this roughly doubles the number of LLM metric data points emitted. If your metrics backend is a managed service billed by data volume or storage, check its pricing before enabling.

collapseEphemeralSessions recognizes two session-key shapes commonly produced by recurring background work: a trailing per-run identifier after :run: (e.g. a cron job's per-run session key), and a trailing per-run identifier after an underscore (e.g. an internal-session-effect turn's key). When enabled, metrics for a matching session key are labeled with the stable part only, instead of a fresh identifier every run — so a "tokens by session" dashboard panel shows one row per job instead of one row per run. Traces and logs are unaffected and always carry the full, per-run session key for drill-down. Default false: existing dashboards keep working unmodified unless you opt in.

main below is a placeholder, not a special value. agent:main:... is only an example session key — main is whatever agent id your openclaw.json happens to use (agents.entries.<agentId>), chosen at setup and renameable later. OpenClaw's setup wizard commonly defaults the first agent to the id main, which is why examples throughout this project's docs use it, but nothing in this plugin's code — or in the rules below — treats that string as literal or implicit. The matching rules operate purely on the trailing suffix shape; whatever precedes it (agent id, channel, job id) is left untouched regardless of what it says.

Exact rules implemented (src/metric-session-key.ts), checked in this order, first match wins — everything else in the key before the matched suffix is left untouched:

  1. A trailing :run:<uuid> is stripped, where <uuid> is a standard 8-4-4-4-12 hex UUID (case-insensitive). This is the shape a recurring cron job's per-run session key carries. 
    agent:main:cron:ff729cdc-1234-5678-9abc-def012345678:run:28c489cb-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd
→ agent:main:cron:ff729cdc-1234-5678-9abc-def012345678
  2. A trailing _<uuid> is stripped, same UUID shape, when it isn't an internal-session-effects: session (rule 3 below is more permissive for those). 
    agent:main:internal-session-effects:skill-workshop-review_a737fdf6-1111-2222-3333-444444444444
→ agent:main:internal-session-effects:skill-workshop-review
  3. For internal-session-effects: session keys specifically, two looser variants also collapse, because real per-run IDs observed live for this session type aren't always standard UUIDs (some have 6 dash-separated hex groups, not 5):
  4. A trailing _<opaque-id> where <opaque-id> is any run of hex digits and dashes (not only a strict UUID): 
    agent:main:internal-session-effects:skill-workshop-review_f54ebfff-d4e5-4969-8c27-87-35c6acc9e5a6bf79
→ agent:main:internal-session-effects:skill-workshop-review
  5. When there's no label before the per-run id at all (nothing to anchor an _ on), a bare hex-and-dash tail directly after the marker's own trailing : collapses to the marker itself: 
    agent:main:internal-session-effects:55d1aba4-57f5-4983-8388-8c9cbf2dd7c9-da3b886ec4001009
→ agent:main:internal-session-effects

Deliberately left uncollapsed — the match is positional (end of string only), never "any UUID anywhere," so a UUID that's a stable identifier rather than a per-run one is untouched:

agent:main:channel:ff729cdc-1234-5678-9abc-def012345678        (a bare trailing UUID, no :run:/_ separator — a channel/job ID)
agent:main:cron:ff729cdc-1234-5678-9abc-def012345678:run:latest (:run: present, but "latest" isn't UUID-shaped)
agent:main:telegram:direct:12345                                (no ephemeral suffix of any recognized shape)

enableByModelMetrics is the feature to reach for when you need a metric that's reliably rate-able, regardless of how often a session recurs — see Limitations for the full comparison with collapseEphemeralSessions (which can incidentally help the common recurring-cron case too, but isn't guaranteed to) and for the one remaining gap in enableByModelMetrics itself. Default false — enabling it roughly doubles the number of LLM metric data points this plugin emits, which has a direct cost impact on a metrics backend billed by data volume or storage.

docs.title: Per-Signal Endpoints (multi-backend fan-out)
docs.text:
For backends that expose a separate ingestion URL per signal instead of one shared OTLP endpoint (e.g. IONOS Cloud Observability: Mimir for metrics, Loki for logs, Tempo for traces), set signalEndpoints (and optionally signalHeaders) alongside the existing endpoint/headers. Any signal not listed falls back to the shared endpoint/headers — this is fully backward compatible with existing configs.

Per-signal endpoints are used verbatim — no /v1/<signal> suffix is appended, unlike the shared endpoint (which still gets suffixed for HTTP). This mirrors the OTel spec's distinction between the base OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (suffixed) and the signal-specific OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_{TRACES,METRICS,LOGS}_ENDPOINT variables (used as-is). It's also required to express real per-signal backend shapes that don't follow a fixed suffix rule — e.g. IONOS's own three pipelines each want a differently-shaped complete URL:

{
  "plugins": {
    "entries": {
      "otel-observability": {
        "enabled": true,
        "config": {
          "protocol": "http",
          "signalEndpoints": {
            "metrics": "https://<pipeline-id>-metrics.<tenant>.monitoring.<region>.ionos.com/otlp/v1/metrics",
            "traces": "https://<pipeline-id>-traces.<tenant>.tracing.<region>.ionos.com/v1/traces",
            "logs": "https://<pipeline-id>-logs.<tenant>.logging.<region>.ionos.com/<tag>"
          },
          "signalHeaders": {
            "metrics": { "APIKEY": "<metrics-pipeline-key>" },
            "traces": { "APIKEY": "<traces-pipeline-key>" },
            "logs": { "APIKEY": "<logs-pipeline-key>" }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

Note IONOS's traces endpoint has no /otlp prefix (unlike metrics), and logs ends in the pipeline's own /<tag> path rather than /v1/logs — since overrides are verbatim, both are expressible even though they don't follow the same shape as each other or as the shared endpoint's suffix rule.

signalHeaders replaces headers entirely for that signal (it is not merged) — set the full header set for that signal's backend, including any shared headers you still need.

If only some signals need their own endpoint, list only those — the rest keep using the shared endpoint/headers:

{
  "plugins": {
    "entries": {
      "otel-observability": {
        "enabled": true,
        "config": {
          "endpoint": "https://otlp-collector.example.com",
          "signalEndpoints": {
            "logs": "https://logs-only-backend.example.com/otlp"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Log Filtering (logConfig)
docs.text:
With logs: true, every line this plugin logs through the gateway logger (the [otel] ... lines, including debug/info lines) is also exported as an OTLP log record. logConfig controls which of those lines get exported. It only affects OTLP export — the gateway's own console/journal output is unchanged.

{
  "plugins": {
    "load": { "paths": ["~/.openclaw/plugins/otel-observability"] },
    "entries": {
      "otel-observability": {
        "enabled": true,
        "hooks": { "allowConversationAccess": true },
        "config": {
          "logs": true,
          "logConfig": {
            "excludeLevels": ["debug", "trace"],
            "excludeMessagePatterns": ["Registered "],
            "filters": [
              { "field": "message", "pattern": "pipeline active", "action": "include" },
              { "field": "level", "pattern": "info", "action": "exclude" }
            ]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

This example drops all debug/trace records and the per-hook Registered ... lines, then — via filters — drops every other info record except the Observability pipeline active startup confirmation. Warnings and errors are still exported.

Field Type Description excludeLevels string[] Drop records at these levels (trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal). Case-insensitive. The usual way to mute noisy debug/info output. excludeLoggers string[] Drop records whose logger name contains any of these strings (case-insensitive substring match). excludeMessagePatterns string[] Drop records whose message contains any of these strings (case-insensitive substring match). filters object[] Ordered rules, each { "field": "logger" \| "message" \| "level" \| "type", "pattern": "<substring>", "action": "exclude" \| "include" }. The first rule whose pattern matches decides: exclude drops the record, include keeps it and skips the remaining rules. Rules with an unknown field or action are ignored. enabled boolean Parsed but currently has no effect. To turn off log export, set "logs": false instead.

Order of evaluation: excludeLevels, then excludeLoggers, then excludeMessagePatterns — any match drops the record — and only then filters. An include rule therefore can't rescue a record that one of the three exclude* lists already dropped. A record matching nothing is exported.

Unlike the trace/metric settings, logs and logConfig changes can take effect through a plugin reload (see Not hot-reloadable below).

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
The plugin's own config (plugins.entries.otel-observability.config) does not fall back to environment variables. endpoint, protocol, serviceName, and every other option above come only from the config file, falling back to the defaults in the table above — setting OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT or OTEL_SERVICE_NAME has no effect on the plugin's exporters.

Environment variables are read only by the optional ESM preload (instrumentation/preload.mjs, loaded via NODE_OPTIONS="--import ..."), which runs before OpenClaw parses plugin config and sets up its own trace exporter for Traceloop LLM-client spans:

Variable Read by Description OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT preload only OTLP/HTTP base endpoint for the preload's trace exporter (default http://localhost:4318; /v1/traces is appended). OTEL_SERVICE_NAME preload only service.name for the preload's spans (default openclaw-gateway). OPENCLAW_OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT preload only Legacy single-boolean flag for Traceloop content capture. true enables prompt/completion text on LLM-client spans. See captureContent (gateway-launch setting). OPENCLAW_OTEL_CONTENT_POLICY preload only Granular policy JSON (ISI-1000). When set, takes precedence over the legacy boolean. Same shape as the plugin's captureContent object form.

OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL is not read by either — the preload always exports OTLP/HTTP (protobuf). If you use the preload, set these to match the plugin config so both exporters send to the same place. The plugin's start() phase overwrites OPENCLAW_OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT/OPENCLAW_OTEL_CONTENT_POLICY in its own process environment from the plugin config, so subprocesses it spawns inherit the plugin's policy.

docs.title: Trace Sampling
docs.text:
The plugin exports 100% of traces by default. For high-traffic gateways this can be tuned down with the sampleRate option (0.0–1.0):

{
  "plugins": {
    "load": { "paths": ["~/.openclaw/plugins/otel-observability"] },
    "entries": {
      "otel-observability": {
        "enabled": true,
        "hooks": { "allowConversationAccess": true },
        "config": {
          "sampleRate": 0.1
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

Semantics:

  • sampleRate omitted — the SDK default sampler (parentbased_always_on) is used. The plugin does not construct its own sampler; nothing sampler-related appears in the boot log.
  • sampleRate: 1.0 — the plugin explicitly constructs ParentBased(TraceIdRatio(1.0)). Behaviourally equivalent to always-on, but the boot log reports sampler=parentbased_traceidratio(1) so operators can confirm the plugin took the sampling code path.
  • 0.0 — drop every trace: no spans are recorded or exported. Metrics and logs are unaffected.
  • Any value in between — keep that fraction of root traces.

Sampling is head-based and parent-respecting: the plugin wires a ParentBasedSampler around a TraceIdRatioBasedSampler. The root span of a trace makes the sampling decision based on the trace ID; child spans inherit the parent's decision so distributed traces stay coherent and you never see "half a trace".

Invalid values (negative, > 1, NaN, non-numeric, null, plain object) are ignored and the SDK default (parentbased_always_on) is used instead. The plugin emits a [otel] Ignoring invalid sampleRate=… warn-level log line whenever it drops a present-but-invalid value, so silent typos like "sampleRate": "0.5" (string) or 1.5 (out-of-range) are visible in operator logs instead of quietly disabling head-based sampling.

docs.title: Precedence vs. OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER env vars
docs.text:
OpenTelemetry SDKs typically read the OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER and OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG environment variables to choose a default sampler. This plugin does not. When sampleRate is set in plugin config, the plugin builds the sampler directly (ParentBased(TraceIdRatio(sampleRate))) and the env vars have no effect on the plugin's tracer provider. When sampleRate is omitted, the plugin omits the sampler key entirely so the SDK's default (parentbased_always_on) applies — and even in that case, the plugin does not propagate OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER to its provider.

Operators migrating from other OTel SDKs should configure sampling via plugins.entries.otel-observability.config.sampleRate rather than the env vars. The precedence is:

Configuration Effective sampler sampleRate set (any valid value) ParentBased(TraceIdRatio(sampleRate)) — env vars ignored sampleRate omitted; OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER set SDK default (parentbased_always_on) — env vars ignored sampleRate omitted; no env vars SDK default (parentbased_always_on) sampleRate present but invalid (e.g. "0.5" string, 1.5) SDK default — plugin emits a logger.warn diagnostic

docs.title: captureContent (gateway-launch setting)
docs.text:
The plugin exposes a captureContent field in plugins.entries.otel-observability.config. It accepts either:

  • a single boolean — true turns every capture category on, false turns every category off (legacy shape, kept for backwards compatibility), or
  • a granular ContentCapturePolicy object with six independent flags:
Flag Span attribute(s) What is captured inputMessages gen_ai.input.messages + openclaw.content.input_message (request span), openclaw.content.prompt / openclaw.content.messages (agent.turn span), gen_ai.prompt.prompt_filter_results (LLM-client span) Inbound user message + the prompt and message history fed to the LLM outputMessages gen_ai.output.messages + openclaw.content.output_message (message.sent span), gen_ai.completion.content_filter_results (LLM-client span) Outbound assistant reply text toolInputs openclaw.content.tool_input (execute_tool span) Full tool-call input arguments (JSON-stringified, capped at 8192 UTF-16 code units) toolOutputs openclaw.content.tool_output (execute_tool span) Tool-call result text (text parts of the result message, capped at 8192 UTF-16 code units) toolErrorMessages openclaw.tool.error_preview (execute_tool span, failure paths only) Bounded, redacted preview of the tool error text (redacted, then capped at 1024 chars). Default differs — see the note below systemPrompt gen_ai.system_instructions + openclaw.content.system_prompt (agent.turn span) System prompt text

The stable gen_ai.* content keys (ISI-1605, schema 1.4.0, shipped in 0.8.0) are emitted alongside the legacy openclaw.content.* mirrors — both share the same policy gate and the same redact-before-truncate funnel (8192 UTF-16 code units, surrogate-safe). The gen_ai.* keys light up Dynatrace AI Observability prompt/response rendering; see Dynatrace → AI Observability. gen_ai.system_instructions carries the system-prompt text and is intentionally distinct from gen_ai.provider.name (provider identity).

⚠️ toolErrorMessages default is a special case. Every other flag defaults off. toolErrorMessages also defaults off when captureContent is omitted or set to the boolean false, but defaults on whenever captureContent is supplied as an object — error text is operational data, a different privacy class from full prompt/response capture. Set { "toolErrorMessages": false } to opt out explicitly.

captureContent value toolErrorMessages → error_preview omitted entirely off false off true on object, e.g. { "toolInputs": true } on (defaults to true when not named) object { "toolErrorMessages": false } off (explicit opt-out)

LLM-client spans emitted by Traceloop (@traceloop/instrumentation-anthropic, @traceloop/instrumentation-openai) still respect the legacy single-boolean Traceloop flag. The plugin derives it from the policy as inputMessages || outputMessages || systemPrompt — the three categories that map to prompt/completion text.

⚠️ Direction selection only applies to the plugin's own spans. Traceloop's traceContent is a single boolean with no input/output distinction, so enabling any of inputMessages, outputMessages, or systemPrompt causes Traceloop LLM-client spans to record both gen_ai.prompt.*.content and gen_ai.completion.*.content. The openclaw.content.* attributes on the plugin's hook-surface spans do honor each flag in isolation — e.g., { inputMessages: true } will record openclaw.content.input_message but not openclaw.content.output_message. If you need strict one-direction capture without completions landing on LLM-client spans, leave every LLM-content flag off and capture from the hook surface only (or filter gen_ai.completion.*.content at the OTel Collector). See Privacy: captureContent.

Default: false (every flag off, privacy-first). See github issue #15 for the motivating report and ISI-1000 for the granular policy.

docs.title: Not hot-reloadable
docs.text:
captureContent is a gateway-launch setting, not a hot-reloadable plugin option, because the ESM preload (instrumentation/preload.mjs) instantiates AnthropicInstrumentation and OpenAIInstrumentation before OpenClaw parses plugin config. Changing the value in openclaw.json mid-run has no effect until the next gateway restart.

The telemetry providers themselves are also preserved across config hot-reload. OpenClaw calls the plugin service stop() before register() during reload; this plugin treats stop() as a non-destructive drain and calls forceFlush() instead of shutdown() so the live TracerProvider/MeterProvider keep exporting spans and metrics after reload.

Because the runtime is reused, changes to telemetry-affecting fields do not take effect until a full gateway restart:

  • endpoint
  • headers
  • protocol
  • serviceName
  • traces
  • metrics
  • sampleRate
  • metricsIntervalMs
  • resourceAttributes
  • signalEndpoints
  • signalHeaders
  • preload-backed content capture (captureContent for Traceloop LLM-client spans)

This is intentional: stale telemetry config is preferable to dropping all post-reload spans. Restart the gateway after changing any of those fields. The log pipeline is rebuilt during service stop()/register() reloads, so logs and logConfig can take effect through the plugin reload path.

docs.title: openclaw.otel.preExit
docs.text:
The plugin publishes a loose pre-exit contract for OpenClaw code paths that call process.exit() before the BatchSpanProcessor export interval fires:

const preExit = globalThis[Symbol.for("openclaw.otel.preExit")];
if (typeof preExit === "function") await preExit();

The plugin sets the symbol to a non-destructive flush function during telemetry initialization and clears it from shutdown(). CLI exit handlers own calling it before forced exit.

docs.title: How to enable content capture
docs.text:
The preload reads two env vars and picks the granular one whenever it is set:

  • OPENCLAW_OTEL_CONTENT_POLICY — granular policy as JSON. Preferred.
  • OPENCLAW_OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT — legacy single boolean. Fallback.

docs.title: All-on (legacy boolean)
docs.text:
OPENCLAW_OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true \
  NODE_OPTIONS="--import /path/to/openclaw-observability-plugin/instrumentation/preload.mjs" \
  openclaw gateway start

{
  "plugins": {
    "entries": {
      "otel-observability": {
        "enabled": true,
        "config": {
          "captureContent": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Granular (recommended)
docs.text:
Enable only what you actually need. For example, capture tool inputs/outputs for debugging without recording user prompts:

OPENCLAW_OTEL_CONTENT_POLICY='{"toolInputs":true,"toolOutputs":true}' \
  NODE_OPTIONS="--import /path/to/openclaw-observability-plugin/instrumentation/preload.mjs" \
  openclaw gateway start

{
  "plugins": {
    "entries": {
      "otel-observability": {
        "enabled": true,
        "config": {
          "captureContent": {
            "toolInputs": true,
            "toolOutputs": true
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

Or via systemd:

[Service]
Environment=OPENCLAW_OTEL_CONTENT_POLICY={"toolInputs":true,"toolOutputs":true}
Environment=NODE_OPTIONS=--import /path/to/openclaw-observability-plugin/instrumentation/preload.mjs
ExecStart=/usr/bin/openclaw gateway start

docs.title: Mismatch warning
docs.text:
If the plugin config and the preload-time env vars disagree about whether LLM-client content capture is on, the plugin logs a warning at start():

[otel] captureContent policy resolves traceContent=true but the preload resolved
OPENCLAW_OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT=false at gateway launch. Traceloop LLM-client
spans will use the preload's value. Set OPENCLAW_OTEL_CONTENT_POLICY='{"inputMessages":true}'
(or OPENCLAW_OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true) in the gateway's environment before
starting (see docs/security/privacy.md).

Fix by setting the env var and restarting the gateway. The plugin's own hook-surface content attributes (openclaw.content.*) are not affected by this warning — they are evaluated against the live plugin config and so are always consistent with the running policy.

docs.title: Privacy guidance
docs.text: Leave captureContent at false unless you control the backend and understand the implications. See Privacy: captureContent for a fuller treatment.

docs.title: Applying Changes
docs.text:
After modifying trace/metric provider configuration:

openclaw gateway restart

Plugin hot reload can apply log pipeline changes (logs and logConfig), but it does not rebuild the trace or metric providers listed above.

docs.title: Configuration Not Applied?
docs.text:
Check the current config:

cat ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json | jq '.plugins.entries["otel-observability"]'

Also confirm plugins.load.paths points at your clone: jq '.plugins.load'.

docs.title: Invalid Config Errors?
docs.text:
Validate JSON syntax:

cat ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json | jq .

docs.title: Endpoint Unreachable?
docs.text:
Test connectivity against your configured endpoint (append /v1/traces for HTTP — gRPC and signalEndpoints overrides are used verbatim, no suffix):

curl -v <your-endpoint>/v1/traces   # e.g. https://otlp-collector.example.com/v1/traces, or http://localhost:4318/v1/traces for a local collector

docs.title: Development
docs.text: How to develop, test, and contribute to the plugin.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
# Clone
git clone https://github.com/th-m-vogel/openclaw-observability-plugin.git
cd openclaw-observability-plugin

# Install dependencies and build (the gateway loads the compiled dist/, see below)
npm ci
npm run build

Then point OpenClaw at your working copy the same way every other doc does — via plugins.load.paths in ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json (see Getting Started for the full entry, including the required hooks.allowConversationAccess):

{
  "plugins": {
    "load": { "paths": ["/path/to/openclaw-observability-plugin"] },
    "entries": {
      "otel-observability": {
        "enabled": true,
        "hooks": { "allowConversationAccess": true },
        "config": { "endpoint": "http://localhost:4318" }
      }
    }
  }
}

# Restart gateway to pick up the plugin
openclaw gateway restart

docs.title: 1. Make Changes
docs.text: Edit the TypeScript files in src/ or index.ts.

docs.title: 2. Rebuild and Restart Gateway
docs.text:
The gateway loads the compiled dist/index.js (the openclaw.runtimeExtensions entry in package.json), not the TypeScript source, so rebuild after every change:

npm run build
openclaw gateway restart

docs.title: 3. Verify
docs.text:
# Check plugin loaded
openclaw otel

# Check gateway logs for [otel] messages
tail -f ~/.openclaw/gateway.log | grep otel

docs.title: 4. Test with Debug Exporter
docs.text:
For quick development, use the collector's debug exporter to see spans in stdout:

docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f otel-collector

Every exported span/metric will appear in the collector logs.

docs.title: Type Checking and Tests
docs.text:
npm run typecheck
npm test

CI runs npm run typecheck, npm run build, and npm test.

Note

The plugin uses OpenClaw's plugin API via any types since the SDK types aren't published separately yet. Once openclaw/plugin-sdk is published, we'll add proper type imports.

docs.title: Testing Locally Without a Backend
docs.text:
You can run with just the debug exporter (no Dynatrace/Grafana needed):

  1. Edit collector/otel-collector-config.yaml:

    service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [debug]  # Remove dynatrace exporter

  2. Start the collector: docker compose up -d

  3. Watch spans: docker compose logs -f otel-collector
  4. Send messages to your OpenClaw agent — you'll see spans appear in the logs

docs.title: Adding New Metrics
docs.text:
1. Define the instrument in src/telemetry.ts:

    // In OtelCounters interface
myNewMetric: Counter;

// In initTelemetry()
myNewMetric: meter.createCounter("openclaw.my.new_metric", {
  description: "Description of what this measures",
  unit: "unit",
}),

  2. Record values in src/hooks.ts (hook-sourced) or src/diagnostics.ts (diagnostic-event-sourced):

    telemetry.counters.myNewMetric.add(1, { "attribute.key": "value" });

  3. Document in docs/telemetry/metrics.md

docs.title: Adding New Spans
docs.text:
1. Use the tracer in src/hooks.ts:

    const span = tracer.startSpan("openclaw.my.operation", {
  kind: SpanKind.INTERNAL,
  attributes: {
    "openclaw.my.attribute": "value",
  },
});

// ... do work ...

span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.OK });
span.end();

  2. Document in docs/telemetry/traces.md

# Install MkDocs (one-time)
pip install mkdocs-material

mkdocs serve

mkdocs build

mkdocs gh-deploy

docs.title: Cutting a release
docs.text:
This fork is not published to npm (see README → Quick start). To cut a release:

# Bump version in package.json and openclaw.plugin.json
# Add a section to CHANGELOG.md
git tag v0.X.0 && git push origin v0.X.0

Users install by cloning the repo at that tag and loading it by path — see README → Quick start for the full steps.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository
  2. Create a feature branch: git checkout -b feature/my-feature
  3. Make your changes
  4. Run the checks CI runs: npm run typecheck, npm run build, and npm test (see CONTRIBUTING.md)
  5. Test with a local collector
  6. Submit a pull request

docs.title: Commit Convention
docs.text:
Use conventional commits:

  • feat: add new metric for session duration
  • fix: handle missing tool name in hook
  • docs: update Dynatrace setup guide
  • refactor: simplify config parsing

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Get OpenTelemetry observability for your OpenClaw AI agents.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• OpenClaw v2026.9.9 or later (see minOpenClawVersion in openclaw.plugin.json — raised from v2026.9.8 once the ISI-9700 undefined-rejection crash regression (openclaw/openclaw#162031) shipped a core fix in this release, see docs/limitations.md)
  • An OTLP endpoint (local collector, Dynatrace, Grafana, etc.)

docs.title: Option 1: Official Diagnostics Plugin (Recommended Start)
docs.text: The fastest way to get observability. No installation needed — just configure.

docs.title: Step 1: Add Configuration
docs.text:
Add to your ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json:

{
  "diagnostics": {
    "enabled": true,
    "otel": {
      "enabled": true,
      "endpoint": "https://otlp-collector.example.com",
      "serviceName": "openclaw-gateway",
      "traces": true,
      "metrics": true,
      "logs": true
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Step 2: Restart Gateway
docs.text: openclaw gateway restart

docs.title: Step 3: Verify
docs.text:
Send a message to your agent and check your backend for:

  • Metrics (emitted by diagnostics-otel): openclaw.tokens, openclaw.cost.usd, openclaw.run.duration_ms
  • Traces: openclaw.model.usage, openclaw.message.processed
  • Logs: Gateway logs with severity and code location

Option 2 (this repo's plugin) emits a different metric set: openclaw.llm.tokens.{total,prompt,completion}, openclaw.llm.cost.usd, and the OTel stable gen_ai.* set. Use one option or the other, not both — see Don't run both plugins at once.

docs.title: Option 2: Custom Hook-Based Plugin (Deeper Tracing)
docs.text: For connected traces and per-tool-call visibility, add the custom plugin.

docs.title: Step 1: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
mkdir -p ~/.openclaw/plugins && cd ~/.openclaw/plugins
git clone --branch v0.12.0 https://github.com/th-m-vogel/openclaw-observability-plugin.git otel-observability

docs.title: Step 2: Install Dependencies and Build
docs.text:
cd otel-observability
npm ci && npm run build

The gateway loads the compiled dist/index.js, not the TypeScript source directly — dist/ isn't checked into the repo, so this build step is required, not optional. Re-run it after every git pull that updates this plugin.

docs.title: Step 3: Configure OpenClaw
docs.text:
Add to your ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json:

{
  "plugins": {
    "load": {
      "paths": ["~/.openclaw/plugins/otel-observability"]
    },
    "entries": {
      "otel-observability": {
        "enabled": true,
        "config": {
          "endpoint": "https://otlp-collector.example.com",
          "protocol": "http",
          "serviceName": "openclaw-gateway"
        },
        "hooks": {
          "allowConversationAccess": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

Required for OpenClaw ≥ 2026.4.23. Path-loaded (non-bundled) plugins must explicitly opt in to conversation typed hooks. Without hooks.allowConversationAccess: true, OpenClaw silently drops the registrations for before_model_resolve, llm_input, llm_output, before_agent_finalize, agent_end, before_agent_reply, and before_agent_run. The plugin still prints its [otel] Registered ... hook (via api.on) banners but the handlers never fire, so no openclaw.request / openclaw.agent.turn spans reach your backend. See github issue #20 and the troubleshooting section below.

Note: Custom plugin settings live under plugins.entries.otel-observability.config. OpenClaw's built-in diagnostics exporter uses a separate diagnostics.otel block; do not mix the two config surfaces.

docs.title: Step 4: Clear Cache and Restart
docs.text:
rm -rf /tmp/jiti
systemctl --user restart openclaw-gateway
# Or: openclaw gateway restart

docs.title: Step 5: Verify Connected Traces
docs.text:
First, confirm the plugin is wired into the gateway. Tail the gateway log during startup:

journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway -f | grep -E '\[otel\]'

You should see these lines during register() (before the gateway accepts traffic). The plugin logs one Registered ... line per hook — about 30 in total — so this is an abbreviated excerpt, not the full list:

[otel] Registered message_received hook (via api.on)
[otel] Registered session_start hook (via api.on)
...
[otel] Registered before_model_resolve hook (via api.on)
...
[otel] Registered agent_end hook (via api.on)
...
[otel] Registered command event hooks (via api.registerHook)
[otel] Registered gateway:startup hook (via api.registerHook)
[otel] Telemetry + hooks initialized at register() (runner-compatible)

Then, during start() (after the gateway is ready):

[otel] Starting OpenTelemetry observability (gateway-only init)...
[otel] ✅ Observability pipeline active (gateway-side)
[otel]   Traces=true Metrics=true Logs=true
[otel]   Endpoint=https://otlp-collector.example.com (http, shared default)
[otel]   Effective endpoints: traces=https://otlp-collector.example.com metrics=https://otlp-collector.example.com logs=https://otlp-collector.example.com

The Effective endpoints line shows each signal's resolved base endpoint, including any signalEndpoints override (see Configuration). For the shared endpoint over HTTP, the exporters append /v1/traces, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs to it; overrides are used verbatim.

Now send a message that triggers tool calls (e.g., "read my AGENTS.md file"). On each inbound message, info-level log lines confirm hooks are firing:

[otel] Root span started: session=<sessionKey>, spanId=<spanId>, storeSize=<n>
[otel] Agent turn span started: agent=<agentId>, session=<sessionKey>

In your backend you should see a connected trace:

openclaw.request
└── openclaw.agent.turn
    └── execute_tool Read

docs.title: Don't run both plugins at once
docs.text: The official diagnostics-otel plugin and this one both initialize the OpenTelemetry SDK and register the global tracer/meter provider — running both at the same time means whichever registers second silently loses (or both end up sharing one provider with mismatched resource/endpoint config), not clean combined coverage. Pick one: the official plugin covers gateway-level health (queues, webhooks, log forwarding); this plugin covers connected per-request tracing, per-tool-call spans, and token/cost metrics. See Limitations for the full reasoning.

docs.title: Local OTel Collector
docs.text:
1. Install: 

    # Ubuntu/Debian
wget https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/releases/download/v0.144.0/otelcol-contrib_0.144.0_linux_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i otelcol-contrib_0.144.0_linux_amd64.deb

  2. Configure (/etc/otelcol-contrib/config.yaml): 

    receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318

processors:
  batch:

exporters:
  debug:
    verbosity: detailed
  # Add your backend exporter

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [debug]
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [debug]
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [debug]

  3. Start: 

    sudo systemctl start otelcol-contrib

docs.title: Dynatrace (Direct)
docs.text:
No collector needed. Plugin config (Option 2):

{
  "plugins": {
    "load": { "paths": ["~/.openclaw/plugins/otel-observability"] },
    "entries": {
      "otel-observability": {
        "enabled": true,
        "hooks": { "allowConversationAccess": true },
        "config": {
          "endpoint": "https://{environment-id}.live.dynatrace.com/api/v2/otlp",
          "headers": {
            "Authorization": "Api-Token {your-token}"
          },
          "serviceName": "openclaw-gateway",
          "traces": true,
          "metrics": true,
          "logs": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

If you're using Option 1 (the official plugin) instead, the same endpoint/headers values go in its diagnostics.otel block.

Required scopes: metrics.ingest, logs.ingest, openTelemetryTrace.ingest

docs.title: Grafana Cloud
docs.text:
Plugin config (Option 2):

{
  "plugins": {
    "load": { "paths": ["~/.openclaw/plugins/otel-observability"] },
    "entries": {
      "otel-observability": {
        "enabled": true,
        "hooks": { "allowConversationAccess": true },
        "config": {
          "endpoint": "https://otlp-gateway-{region}.grafana.net/otlp",
          "headers": {
            "Authorization": "Basic {base64(instanceId:apiKey)}"
          },
          "serviceName": "openclaw-gateway",
          "traces": true,
          "metrics": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

If you're using Option 1 (the official plugin) instead, the same endpoint/headers values go in its diagnostics.otel block.

docs.title: No data appearing?
docs.text:
1. Check Gateway logs: 

    journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway -f

  2. Verify endpoint is reachable (your configured endpoint, with /v1/traces appended for HTTP): 

    curl -v <your-endpoint>/v1/traces   # e.g. https://otlp-collector.example.com/v1/traces, or http://localhost:4318/v1/traces for a local collector

  3. Check the plugin config (Option 2): 

    cat ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json | jq '.plugins.entries["otel-observability"]'
    If you're using Option 1 (the official plugin), check jq '.diagnostics' instead.

docs.title: Custom plugin not loading?
docs.text:
1. Check plugin discovery: 

    openclaw plugins list

  2. Clear jiti cache: 

    rm -rf /tmp/jiti

  3. Check for TypeScript errors in Gateway logs

docs.title: Traces not connected?
docs.text: The custom plugin requires messages to flow through the normal pipeline. Heartbeats and some internal events may not have full trace context.

docs.title: Hooks register but never fire
docs.text:
Symptom: Gateway logs [otel] ✅ Observability pipeline active (gateway-side), but no openclaw.request or execute_tool * spans reach your backend when you send messages.

Cause (pre-PR #6): Earlier builds registered typed hooks from inside the async service.start() phase. OpenClaw snapshots typed hooks at plugin registration time — ~30 s before start() runs — so the gateway never saw the 15 hook listeners. Tracked as ISI-515.

Fix: Upgrade to a build that includes PR #6. Hooks are now registered synchronously in register() and resolve the telemetry runtime through a lazy getter.

How to confirm hooks are live:

  1. During gateway startup, look for the Registered ... lines from register() — one per hook, about 30 in total. A representative subset: 

    [otel] Registered message_received hook (via api.on)
[otel] Registered before_model_resolve hook (via api.on)
[otel] Registered tool_result_persist hook (via api.on)
[otel] Registered agent_end hook (via api.on)
[otel] Registered command event hooks (via api.registerHook)
[otel] Registered gateway:startup hook (via api.registerHook)
    If these are missing, either the plugin is not loaded — recheck plugins.load.paths and clear /tmp/jiti — or it was loaded in a non-full registration mode, in which case the log shows [otel] Non-full registration (<mode>) detected — skipping telemetry init instead. That line is expected for one-shot CLI commands and internal discovery passes; the gateway's own registration should not produce it.

  2. Send a real message through the pipeline. These lines are logged at info level, so no debug logging is needed: 

    [otel] Root span started: session=<sessionKey>, spanId=<spanId>, storeSize=<n>
[otel] Agent turn span started: agent=<agentId>, session=<sessionKey>
    If registration lines are present but these are missing, the gateway is not firing hooks for that event path (e.g., heartbeats skip message_received).

  3. Verify the OTLP endpoint is reachable: 

    curl -v <your-endpoint>/v1/traces   # e.g. https://otlp-collector.example.com/v1/traces, or http://localhost:4318/v1/traces for a local collector

See Architecture → Plugin Lifecycle for why the register() vs start() split matters.
