docs.title: Metrics Reference
docs.text:
Metrics use the openclaw.* namespace — plus the two stable OTel GenAI histograms gen_ai.client.token.usage and gen_ai.client.operation.duration — and are exported via OTLP every metricsIntervalMs (default: 30 seconds).

A metric only appears in your backend once something has recorded a value to it, so event-driven metrics (webhooks, cron, failover, memory pressure, ...) stay absent until the matching OpenClaw event actually fires. A core set of counters (LLM requests/errors/tokens, tool calls/errors, messages, session resets, security) is kept alive with a zero-value data point every export interval, carrying the attribute openclaw.idle=true — filter that out (or ignore it, since it adds 0) in queries that group by attribute.

This page covers metrics emitted by this plugin only. For OpenClaw core's own first-party metric catalog (emitted by the official diagnostics-otel plugin — see index for how the two relate), the authoritative reference is OpenClaw core: Model calls and exported metrics. Always check that page (or the core source directly) before assuming a field exists on a diagnostic event — see Limitations for a real example of what happens when that isn't done.

docs.title: LLM Metrics
docs.text:
0.11.0+: openclaw.llm.requests and .duration record once per real model API call, from the model_call_started/model_call_ended hook pair, instead of once per agent turn from the model.usage diagnostic event (a turn may cover several real calls in a tool-use loop).

0.11.0+ (requires OpenClaw v2026.9.8+): openclaw.llm.tokens.* (prompt/completion/total, including the cache_read/cache_write breakdown) also moved to a per-call source — model.call.completed/model.call.error diagnostic events (via onInternalDiagnosticEvent, a different mechanism than the hook pair above). These carry genuine call-scoped usage (observer.usageField()) confirmed since that release; the hook pair itself still carries none. openclaw.llm.cost.usd is unchanged — still once per agent turn, from model.usage — because no per-call cost field exists anywhere in OpenClaw's plugin API. If you're upgrading a dashboard or alert built against pre-0.11.0 semantics: .tokens.* cardinality changed the same way .requests/.duration did (one increment per real call instead of per turn), and so did its labels, to match .requests/.duration exactly: gen_ai.operation.name is now "chat" (was "invoke_agent"), gen_ai.agent.id is now present when known, and gen_ai.provider.name/openclaw.provider are omitted entirely when the provider is unknown (was always set, including to the literal string "unknown"). A panel filtering on the old operation_name="invoke_agent" value will silently stop matching .tokens.* — update it to "chat", the same value .requests/.duration already use. .cost.usd behaves exactly as before, including its labels.

docs.title: collapseEphemeralSessions (metrics only)
docs.text: With collapseEphemeralSessions: true (see Configuration), the gen_ai.conversation.id label on openclaw.llm.requests, .errors, .duration, .tokens.*, and .cost.usd, on gen_ai.client.token.usage and gen_ai.client.operation.duration, and on openclaw.tool.calls, openclaw.tool.duration, and openclaw.tool.approvals — may be a collapsed, stable job-level value instead of the full per-run session key, for session keys matching one of the two recognized ephemeral shapes (see Configuration). Trace spans and log lines are unaffected and always carry the full per-run session key for drill-down. Default false: this label is the raw session key everywhere, same as before this option existed.

docs.title: _by_model metrics (opt-in)
docs.text:
With enableByModelMetrics: true (see Configuration), every per-conversation LLM metric gets an additional _by_model sibling: same value, same attributes, but with gen_ai.conversation.id/gen_ai.agent.id dropped so the series is rate-able even for a one-shot session (see Limitations for the rate()/increase() blind spot this fixes). Default false — enabling it roughly doubles the number of LLM metric data points this plugin emits; if your metrics backend is a managed service billed by data volume or storage, check its pricing before enabling.

This is the feature to reach for when you need a metric that's reliably rate-able, regardless of how often a session recurs. collapseEphemeralSessions can incidentally make a recurring-cron series rate-able too, once it's accumulated more than one sample across multiple runs — but that's a side effect of a dashboard-legibility feature, not guaranteed (a job that runs infrequently relative to metricsIntervalMs, or hasn't run twice yet, is still effectively one-shot even when collapsed). See Limitations for the full comparison, including the one remaining gap in enableByModelMetrics itself (a _by_model series is still born flat on its very first sample per provider+model per gateway process lifetime).

Source metric _by_model sibling openclaw.llm.requests openclaw.llm.requests_by_model openclaw.llm.errors openclaw.llm.errors_by_model openclaw.llm.duration openclaw.llm.duration_by_model openclaw.llm.tokens.total openclaw.llm.tokens.total_by_model openclaw.llm.tokens.prompt openclaw.llm.tokens.prompt_by_model openclaw.llm.tokens.completion openclaw.llm.tokens.completion_by_model openclaw.llm.cost.usd openclaw.llm.cost.usd_by_model gen_ai.client.token.usage (stable semconv) openclaw.genai.client.token.usage_by_model gen_ai.client.operation.duration (stable semconv) openclaw.genai.client.operation.duration_by_model

The two semconv-sourced siblings live in this plugin's own openclaw.* namespace rather than gen_ai.client.*_by_model, so the stable GenAI semconv names stay exactly spec-compliant. Tool metrics (openclaw.tool.*) have the same underlying blind spot but don't have a _by_model sibling yet.

docs.title: openclaw.llm.requests
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit requests Attributes gen_ai.response.model, gen_ai.operation.name (chat), gen_ai.conversation.id, gen_ai.provider.name + openclaw.provider (legacy mirror) when the provider is known, gen_ai.agent.id when known Description Total number of real LLM API calls made

Tracks every call to Anthropic, OpenAI, or any other configured provider — one increment per real call, not per agent turn. Use this to understand request volume over time.

docs.title: openclaw.llm.errors
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit errors Attributes Same as openclaw.llm.requests Description Total number of LLM API errors

Counts failed LLM calls (rate limits, timeouts, invalid requests, etc.). A spike here usually means rate limiting or API issues.

docs.title: openclaw.llm.tokens.total
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit tokens Attributes Same as openclaw.llm.requests Description Total tokens consumed per real model API call (prompt + completion + cache read + cache write)

The primary token-volume metric. Combine with model information to estimate costs (see openclaw.llm.cost.usd for the plugin's own turn-level cost figure). Unlike openclaw.llm.cost.usd, this metric does not need the plugin's own #166289 dedup guard — it comes from model.call.completed/model.call.error, which core itself idempotency-guards per call (a one-shot observer.state.terminalEventEmitted flag), a structurally different and already-safe emission path from model.usage (the event #166289 actually affects).

docs.title: openclaw.llm.tokens.prompt
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit tokens Attributes Same as openclaw.llm.tokens.total, plus token.type (cache_read/cache_write) on the cache-token increments Description Prompt tokens consumed per real model API call

Tracks input tokens. High prompt token counts may indicate large system prompts, long conversation histories, or excessive context injection. Note this grows with real, incremental usage turn-over-turn — in a non-caching provider, each turn in a long conversation legitimately carries more input than the last, since the full history gets resent; that's real billed usage, not double-counting.

docs.title: openclaw.llm.tokens.completion
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit tokens Attributes Same as openclaw.llm.tokens.total Description Completion tokens consumed per real model API call

Tracks output tokens. Useful for understanding response verbosity.

docs.title: openclaw.llm.duration
docs.text:
Type Histogram Unit ms Attributes Same as openclaw.llm.requests Description Real model API call duration in milliseconds

Latency distribution for individual LLM calls (not full agent turns — see openclaw.agent.turn_duration for that). Use percentiles (p50, p95, p99) to understand typical and worst-case latency.

docs.title: openclaw.llm.cost.usd
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit usd Attributes gen_ai.response.model, gen_ai.provider.name, openclaw.provider (legacy mirror), gen_ai.operation.name (invoke_agent), gen_ai.conversation.id Description Estimated LLM cost in USD, once per agent turn

Sourced from OpenClaw core's turn-level model.usage diagnostic event, the only place a cost figure exists in the plugin API — recorded only when core supplies a positive costUsd, and dedup-guarded against the #166289 duplicate dispatch. Missing entirely for session types where core never emits model.usage, and for custom/self-hosted providers core has no price table for — see Limitations. Note the different gen_ai.operation.name from the per-call metrics above (invoke_agent vs chat), and no gen_ai.agent.id.

docs.title: gen_ai.client.token.usage
docs.text:
Type Histogram (stable OTel GenAI semconv) Unit {token} Attributes Same as openclaw.llm.requests, plus gen_ai.token.type (input, output, cache_read, cache_creation) Description Tokens per real model API call, one data point per token type

Same source and timing as openclaw.llm.tokens.* (the model.call.completed/model.call.error diagnostic events).

docs.title: gen_ai.client.operation.duration
docs.text:
Type Histogram (stable OTel GenAI semconv) Unit s Attributes Per-call points: same as openclaw.llm.requests (gen_ai.operation.name = chat). Per-turn points: gen_ai.response.model, gen_ai.operation.name = invoke_agent, gen_ai.agent.id, openclaw.agent.id Description Duration in seconds of both real model calls and whole agent turns

Recorded from two places: once per real call (model_call_ended, same value as openclaw.llm.duration in seconds) and once per agent turn (agent_end, same value as openclaw.agent.turn_duration in seconds). Filter or group by gen_ai.operation.name — mixing the two in one percentile gives a meaningless result.

docs.title: Why can't tokens/cost be per-call too?
docs.text: openclaw.llm.requests/.duration moved to a per-call hook in 0.11.0 because they don't need any usage data — a call either happened or it didn't, and timing is always available. openclaw.llm.tokens.* needed OpenClaw core to tell the plugin how many tokens a given call used; that didn't exist on the obvious-looking hook pair (model_call_started/model_call_ended, which deliberately carries no usage), but does exist, since v2026.9.8, on the separate model.call.completed/model.call.error diagnostic events, which this plugin adopted in 0.11.0. See docs/limitations.md for the full investigation and what's still turn-level only (cost).

docs.title: openclaw.model.failover
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit 1 Attributes openclaw.provider, openclaw.model, openclaw.failover.to_provider, openclaw.failover.to_model, openclaw.failover.reason, openclaw.failover.suspended, openclaw.lane — all optional, present only when the underlying event carries them Description OpenClaw core switched provider/model mid-session (error, rate limit, or routing policy)

Sourced from core's own model.failover trusted diagnostic event (same general dispatch channel as model.usage; see OpenClaw core: Model calls and exported metrics). Useful for catching real incidents as they happen instead of reconstructing them from logs after the fact — e.g. an upstream provider outage triggering an automatic fallback.

docs.title: openclaw.tool.calls
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit calls Attributes gen_ai.tool.name, gen_ai.operation.name (execute_tool), gen_ai.conversation.id Description Total tool invocations

Broken down by tool name. Shows which tools are used most frequently. Carries the per-conversation gen_ai.conversation.id label, so it has the same rate()/increase() one-shot-series caveat as the LLM metrics (and no _by_model-style sibling yet) — see Limitations.

Example attribute values: exec, Read, Write, web_fetch, web_search, browser, memory_search

docs.title: openclaw.tool.errors
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit errors Attributes gen_ai.tool.name Description Total tool execution errors

Broken down by tool name. High error rates on specific tools may indicate configuration issues or external service problems.

docs.title: openclaw.tool.duration
docs.text:
Type Histogram Unit ms Attributes gen_ai.tool.name, gen_ai.conversation.id Description Tool execution duration in milliseconds

How long each tool takes. Useful for identifying slow tools that bottleneck agent turns.

docs.title: openclaw.tool.approvals
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit approvals Attributes gen_ai.tool.name, gen_ai.conversation.id Description Tool calls that required an approval before running

Incremented when a tool call starts with an approval requirement. The approval outcome and wait time are span attributes on the tool span (openclaw.tool.approval.resolution, openclaw.tool.approval.duration_ms), not metrics.

docs.title: openclaw.tool.loop
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit 1 Attributes openclaw.toolName, openclaw.loop.level (warning/critical), openclaw.loop.action (warn/block), openclaw.loop.detector, openclaw.loop.count, optional openclaw.loop.paired_tool Description OpenClaw core detected a repetitive tool-call loop and warned or blocked it

Sourced from core's own tool.loop internal diagnostic event (same general dispatch channel as model.usage; see OpenClaw core: Model calls and exported metrics). openclaw.loop.detector is one of generic_repeat, argument_churn, unknown_tool_repeat, known_poll_no_progress, global_circuit_breaker, or ping_pong. Useful as a runaway-agent safety signal — e.g. catching a stuck skill-workshop session looping on the same tool call instead of making progress — complementing the security-detection layer below.

docs.title: openclaw.skill.used
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit 1 Attributes openclaw.skill.name, openclaw.skill.source, openclaw.skill.activation, optional openclaw.agent, optional openclaw.toolName Description A skill was invoked (via a /command or a bundled Skill tool read)

Sourced from OpenClaw core's own skill.used trusted diagnostic event (same general dispatch channel as model.usage; see OpenClaw core: Model calls and exported metrics). openclaw.skill.source is bundled, workspace, or unknown; openclaw.skill.activation is command or read. openclaw.agent/openclaw.toolName are present only when the underlying event carries them.

docs.title: openclaw.agent.turn_duration
docs.text:
Type Histogram Unit ms Attributes gen_ai.response.model, gen_ai.operation.name (invoke_agent), gen_ai.agent.id, openclaw.agent.id Description Full agent turn duration (LLM + tools + processing)

End-to-end time for a complete agent turn. This is the user-perceived latency.

docs.title: openclaw.agent_turns.active
docs.text:
Type UpDownCounter Unit turns Description Declared but currently never updated

The instrument is created at startup, but no code path increments or decrements it, so it never reports data. Listed here so a name seen in a metrics browser isn't mistaken for a broken pipeline.

docs.title: openclaw.requests.active
docs.text:
Type UpDownCounter Unit requests Description Declared but currently never updated

Same as openclaw.agent_turns.active: created, never recorded to.

docs.title: openclaw.session.resets
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit resets Attributes command.source (from the command:new/command:reset event hooks) or openclaw.session.reset_reason (from the before_reset typed hook) Description Total session resets

Emitted from two different call sites with two different attribute keys — group by whichever one matches the code path you're inspecting; a single query against only one key will undercount.

docs.title: openclaw.sessions.active
docs.text:
Type UpDownCounter Unit sessions Attributes openclaw.session.channel Description Currently active sessions

A gauge-like metric showing the number of active sessions at any point in time — incremented on session_start, decremented on session_end.

docs.title: openclaw.session.stuck
docs.text: Type Counter Unit events Attributes openclaw.session.key Description Core's session.stuck diagnostic event fired

docs.title: openclaw.session.stuck_age_ms
docs.text: Type Histogram Unit ms Attributes openclaw.session.key Description Age of the stuck session when session.stuck fired

docs.title: openclaw.session.long_running
docs.text: Type Counter Unit events Attributes openclaw.session.key Description Core's session.long_running diagnostic event fired

docs.title: openclaw.session.stalled
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit events Attributes openclaw.session.key Description Core's session.stalled diagnostic event fired

These four carry the raw session key as a label (not collapsed by collapseEphemeralSessions), so they're high-cardinality by design — aggregate them away for alerting panels.

docs.title: Queue Metrics
docs.text: All sourced from core's queue.lane.enqueue/queue.lane.dequeue diagnostic events.

docs.title: openclaw.queue.lane.enqueue
docs.text: Type Counter Unit events Attributes openclaw.queue.lane (when present) Description Items added to a queue lane

docs.title: openclaw.queue.lane.dequeue
docs.text: Type Counter Unit events Attributes openclaw.queue.lane (when present) Description Items removed from a queue lane

docs.title: openclaw.queue.depth
docs.text: Type Histogram Unit items Attributes openclaw.queue.lane (when present) Description Lane depth, sampled on every enqueue and dequeue

docs.title: openclaw.queue.wait_ms
docs.text: Type Histogram Unit ms Attributes openclaw.queue.lane (when present) Description Wait time reported on enqueue

docs.title: Gateway Health Metrics
docs.text: Sourced from core's diagnostic.liveness.warning, diagnostic.heartbeat, diagnostic.memory.sample, and diagnostic.memory.pressure diagnostic events. The histograms below carry no attributes.

docs.title: openclaw.liveness.warnings
docs.text: Type Counter Unit events Attributes openclaw.diagnostic.phase Description Core's diagnostic.liveness.warning event fired

docs.title: openclaw.diagnostic.heartbeats
docs.text: Type Counter Unit events Attributes openclaw.diagnostic.phase Description Core's diagnostic.heartbeat event fired

docs.title: openclaw.gateway.* histograms
docs.text:
Metric Unit Recorded from openclaw.gateway.event_loop_delay_p99 ms liveness warnings openclaw.gateway.event_loop_delay_max ms liveness warnings openclaw.gateway.event_loop_utilization 1 liveness warnings openclaw.gateway.cpu_core_ratio 1 liveness warnings openclaw.gateway.work_queued items liveness warnings and heartbeats

Each is recorded only when the triggering event carries the corresponding field.

docs.title: openclaw.memory.pressure
docs.text: Type Counter Unit 1 Attributes openclaw.memory.reason, openclaw.memory.level (each when present) Description Core's diagnostic.memory.pressure event fired

docs.title: openclaw.memory.* histograms
docs.text:
Metric Unit openclaw.memory.rss_bytes By openclaw.memory.heap_used_bytes By openclaw.memory.heap_total_bytes By openclaw.memory.external_bytes By openclaw.memory.array_buffers_bytes By

Recorded from the memory snapshot on both diagnostic.memory.sample and diagnostic.memory.pressure events.

docs.title: openclaw.compaction.count
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit events Attributes openclaw.compaction.reason Description Total context-compaction events

How often the runtime compacts session context. Auto-compaction reports reason="auto". Pairs with the openclaw.compaction span for per-event detail.

docs.title: openclaw.compaction.tokens_reclaimed
docs.text:
Type Histogram Unit {token} Attributes openclaw.compaction.reason Description Tokens reclaimed by a context-compaction event (tokens_before − tokens_after, clamped at 0)

Quantifies how much context each compaction frees. Recorded only when the runtime reports both pre- and post-compaction token counts.

docs.title: openclaw.messages.received
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit messages Description Total inbound messages

Counts messages received from users across all channels. Attribute: openclaw.message.channel.

docs.title: openclaw.messages.sent
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit messages Description Total outbound messages

Counts messages sent by the agent across all channels. Attribute: openclaw.message.channel.

docs.title: Webhook Metrics
docs.text: Sourced from the webhook_received, webhook_processed, and webhook_error hooks. Note the plural webhooks in the counter names and the singular webhook in the histogram names.

docs.title: openclaw.webhooks.received
docs.text: Type Counter Unit events Attributes openclaw.webhook.source, openclaw.webhook.event_type Description Webhooks received

docs.title: openclaw.webhooks.processed
docs.text: Type Counter Unit events Attributes openclaw.webhook.source, openclaw.webhook.event_type Description Webhooks processed successfully

docs.title: openclaw.webhooks.errors
docs.text: Type Counter Unit errors Attributes openclaw.webhook.source, openclaw.webhook.event_type Description Webhook processing errors

docs.title: openclaw.webhook.duration
docs.text: Type Histogram Unit ms Attributes openclaw.webhook.source, openclaw.webhook.event_type Description Webhook processing duration (recorded on success and on error)

docs.title: openclaw.webhook.payload_size
docs.text: Type Histogram Unit bytes Attributes openclaw.webhook.source Description Size of a received webhook payload, when reported

docs.title: Cron Metrics
docs.text: Sourced from the cron_changed and cron_executed hooks.

docs.title: openclaw.cron.changes
docs.text: Type Counter Unit events Attributes openclaw.cron.job_name, openclaw.cron.action Description Cron job definition changes

docs.title: openclaw.cron.executions
docs.text: Type Counter Unit events Attributes openclaw.cron.job_name, openclaw.cron.trigger Description Cron job runs

docs.title: openclaw.cron.errors
docs.text: Type Counter Unit errors Attributes openclaw.cron.job_name Description Failed cron job runs

docs.title: openclaw.cron.duration
docs.text: Type Histogram Unit ms Attributes openclaw.cron.job_name, openclaw.cron.trigger Description Cron job run duration, when reported

docs.title: Sub-agent Metrics
docs.text: Sourced from the subagent_spawned (or legacy subagent_spawning) and subagent_ended hooks.

docs.title: openclaw.subagent.spawns
docs.text: Type Counter Unit events Attributes openclaw.subagent.child_agent_name, openclaw.subagent.spawn_reason Description Sub-agents spawned

docs.title: openclaw.subagent.ended
docs.text: Type Counter Unit events Attributes openclaw.subagent.child_agent_name, openclaw.subagent.success Description Sub-agents finished

docs.title: openclaw.subagent.duration
docs.text: Type Histogram Unit ms Attributes openclaw.subagent.child_agent_name, gen_ai.response.model Description Sub-agent run duration

docs.title: openclaw.security.events
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit events Attributes detection, severity Description Total security events detected across all detection types

The umbrella counter for all security detections. Use detection to filter by type (sensitive_file_access, prompt_injection, dangerous_command) and severity to filter by level (critical, high, warning).

docs.title: openclaw.security.sensitive_file_access
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit events Attributes file_pattern Description Attempts to access sensitive files (credentials, SSH keys, .env, etc.)

Triggers when the agent reads, writes, or edits files matching sensitive patterns (.env, .ssh/, credentials, api_key, etc.). The file_pattern attribute contains the regex source that matched.

docs.title: openclaw.security.prompt_injection
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit events Attributes pattern_count Description Prompt injection attempts detected in inbound messages

Detects social engineering patterns like "ignore previous instructions", fake [SYSTEM] tags, role manipulation ("pretend you are"), and jailbreak attempts. The pattern_count attribute shows how many patterns matched (more = higher confidence).

docs.title: openclaw.security.dangerous_command
docs.text:
Type Counter Unit events Attributes command_type Description Dangerous shell command executions detected

Catches data exfiltration (curl -d, nc -e), destructive commands (rm -rf /, mkfs), privilege escalation (chmod +s), crypto mining (xmrig), and persistence mechanisms (crontab, .bashrc modification). The command_type attribute describes the matched threat.

docs.title: Token Usage Over Time
docs.text:
Track cost by monitoring openclaw.llm.tokens.total over time. In Dynatrace:

timeseries sum(openclaw.llm.tokens.total), by:{gen_ai.response.model}

docs.title: Most Used Tools
docs.text: timeseries sum(openclaw.tool.calls), by:{gen_ai.tool.name}

docs.text: timeseries sum(openclaw.security.sensitive_file_access), by:{file_pattern}

docs.title: Token Usage Attributes
docs.text: Understanding the GenAI token usage attributes in OpenClaw observability.

docs.title: Token Attributes Overview
docs.text:
Attribute Description Cost Impact gen_ai.usage.input_tokens Tokens in the prompt sent to the model Standard input rate gen_ai.usage.output_tokens Tokens in the model's response Higher rate (typically 3-5x input) gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens Tokens read from prompt cache 90% cheaper than input gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens Tokens written to prompt cache 25% more expensive than input

Schema 1.3.0 (ISI-1004) removed the legacy gen_ai.usage.cache_read_tokens / gen_ai.usage.cache_write_tokens / gen_ai.usage.total_tokens keys. Total tokens are now computed as gen_ai.usage.input_tokens + gen_ai.usage.output_tokens; cache reads / writes use the stable cache_read.input_tokens / cache_creation.input_tokens keys.

docs.title: Input Tokens
docs.text:
What counts: Everything you send to the model: - System prompt (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, TOOLS.md, etc.) - Conversation history (all previous messages) - Current user message - Tool definitions and descriptions - Any injected context

Example breakdown: 

System prompt:     ~8,000 tokens (workspace files + tool list)
History:           ~5,000 tokens (previous messages)
Current message:      ~50 tokens (user's question)
─────────────────────────────────
Total input:      ~13,050 tokens

docs.title: Output Tokens
docs.text:
What counts: Everything the model generates: - The assistant's response text - Tool calls (function names + arguments) - Thinking/reasoning (if using extended thinking)

Note: Output tokens are typically 3-5x more expensive than input tokens.

docs.title: Cache Read Tokens
docs.text:
What it is: Anthropic's prompt caching feature. When you send the same prefix (system prompt + early conversation), Claude can reuse a cached version instead of reprocessing it.

When it happens: - Same system prompt across requests - Stable conversation history prefix - Request made within cache TTL (typically 5 minutes)

Cost benefit: Cache reads cost ~90% less than regular input tokens.

Your example: 918,174 cache read tokens means the model reused ~918K tokens from cache instead of reprocessing them. This saved significant cost!

docs.title: Cache Write Tokens
docs.text:
What it is: When new content is added to the cache for future requests.

When it happens: - First request with a new system prompt - Conversation grows beyond previously cached content - Cache TTL expired and content needs re-caching

Cost impact: Cache writes cost ~25% more than regular input tokens, but enable cheaper cache reads on subsequent requests.

Your example: 62,437 cache write tokens means new content was cached for future use.

docs.title: Real-World Example
docs.text:
Your span shows: 

cache_read:   918,174 tokens  (reused from cache — very cheap!)
cache_write:   62,437 tokens  (newly cached — slight premium)
input:            156 tokens  (new content not in cache)
output:        17,831 tokens  (model's response)
─────────────────────────────────
total:        998,598 tokens

What this means:

  1. Large context reuse — 918K tokens were already cached (system prompt + conversation history). You paid ~10% of normal input cost for these.

  2. Incremental caching — 62K new tokens were added to cache. Slightly more expensive now, but future requests can read them cheaply.

  3. Minimal new input — Only 156 tokens were truly "new" input (probably just the latest message).

  4. Reasonable output — 17,831 tokens is a substantial response (maybe code generation or detailed explanation).

docs.title: Illustrative Anthropic API Pricing
docs.text:
The table below is a worked example to show how the cost calculation works, not a live price list — Anthropic's model lineup and rates change over time (the models actually seen in production telemetry for this plugin are the current Claude generation, e.g. claude-sonnet-5, not the 4.5-era names below). Check Anthropic's current pricing for the rates that apply to whatever model you're actually running.

Model Input Output Cache Read Cache Write Opus 4.5 $5/MTok $25/MTok $0.50/MTok $6.25/MTok Sonnet 4.5 $3/MTok $15/MTok $0.30/MTok $3.75/MTok Haiku 4.5 $1/MTok $5/MTok $0.10/MTok $1.25/MTok

(MTok = Million Tokens)

docs.title: Example Cost Breakdown (Opus 4.5)
docs.text:
Token Type Count Rate (per 1M) Cost Cache read 918,174 $0.50 $0.46 Cache write 62,437 $6.25 $0.39 Input 156 $5.00 $0.001 Output 17,831 $25.00 $0.45 Total ~$1.30

Without caching, the same request would cost: - All input at standard rate: (918,174 + 62,437 + 156) × $5/1M = $4.90 - Output: $0.45 - Total without cache: $5.35

Savings from caching: ~76%

docs.text:
Claude Subscription API (OpenClaw uses this) Free: $0 Pay per token Pro: $20/month No monthly fee Max: $100-200/month Billed to API account

Your Claude Pro/Max subscription does NOT cover OpenClaw usage! OpenClaw uses the API, which is billed separately.

docs.title: Why Total Doesn't Equal Sum
docs.text:
You might notice: 

cache_read + cache_write + input + output ≠ a backend's reported total

Adding cache_read.input_tokens + cache_creation.input_tokens + input_tokens + output_tokens may not equal a backend's reported total — different backends count overhead tokens differently. As of schema 1.3.0, OpenClaw no longer emits gen_ai.usage.total_tokens; compute it as gen_ai.usage.input_tokens + gen_ai.usage.output_tokens on the consumer side.

docs.title: Reduce Input Tokens
docs.text:
1. Trim workspace files — Keep AGENTS.md, SOUL.md concise
  2. Use /compact — Summarize long conversations
  3. Prune tool list — Disable unused tools/skills

docs.title: Maximize Cache Hits
docs.text:
1. Stable system prompts — Don't change workspace files frequently
  2. Consistent conversation prefix — Same session = better caching
  3. Heartbeat within TTL — Keep cache warm with periodic requests

docs.title: Control Output
docs.text:
1. Be specific — Vague prompts generate verbose responses
  2. Request concise answers — "Brief answer:" prefix helps
  3. Use appropriate models — Smaller models for simple tasks

docs.title: Monitoring Token Usage
docs.text:
Note: As of 0.11.0+, openclaw_llm_tokens_total (and _prompt/_completion) accumulate per real model API call, not per agent turn — a turn with several tool-use round-trips (like the cache_read/cache_write example above) now produces one increment per call, via the model.call.completed/model.call.error diagnostic events (requires OpenClaw v2026.9.8+). Before 0.11.0 these were turn-aggregated like openclaw_llm_cost_usd still is today. Cost remains turn-level only — there's no per-call cost source anywhere in OpenClaw's plugin API; see docs/limitations.md for why.

One consequence of per-call instrumentation: a conversation carries a unique gen_ai.conversation.id label, so a conversation whose calls all land in the same ~30s metrics-export window (a one-shot cron/background session, or just a fast multi-call burst) produces a single sample with nothing earlier to diff against — rate()/increase() queries show 0 for it even though the value is really there (an instant query finds it fine). See docs/limitations.md for the full mechanism and a query workaround before assuming a panel showing zero means no data arrived.

docs.title: Key Metrics to Watch
docs.text:
# Total tokens right now, by model (instant value, not a rate — avoids the
# one-shot-series blind spot above; see docs/limitations.md)
sum(openclaw_llm_tokens_total) by (gen_ai_response_model)

# Token growth rate for long-running/multi-call sessions (accurate once a
# conversation's calls span more than one export tick)
sum(rate(openclaw_llm_tokens_total[5m])) by (gen_ai_response_model)

# Cache hit ratio (from the gen_ai.client.token.usage histogram)
sum(rate(gen_ai_client_token_usage_sum{gen_ai_token_type="cache_read"}[5m])) /
sum(rate(gen_ai_client_token_usage_sum{gen_ai_token_type=~"cache_read|input"}[5m]))

# Output to input ratio (efficiency)
sum(rate(gen_ai_client_token_usage_sum{gen_ai_token_type="output"}[5m])) /
sum(rate(gen_ai_client_token_usage_sum{gen_ai_token_type="input"}[5m]))

docs.title: Alerting Thresholds
docs.text: Consider alerts for: - Single request > 100K output tokens - Cache hit ratio < 50% - Hourly cost > $X threshold

docs.title: Traces Reference
docs.text:
The plugin generates connected distributed traces using OpenClaw's hook-based plugin API.

This page covers spans emitted by this plugin only. For OpenClaw core's own first-party spans and the full diagnostic event catalog they're built from (emitted by the official diagnostics-otel plugin — see index for how the two relate), see OpenClaw core: Exported spans and diagnostic events.

docs.title: Trace Structure
docs.text:
Every user message produces a trace tree:

openclaw.request (SERVER span — full message lifecycle)
├── openclaw.agent.turn (INTERNAL — LLM processing)
│   ├── gen_ai.usage.input_tokens: 4521
│   ├── gen_ai.usage.output_tokens: 892
│   ├── gen_ai.response.model: claude-opus-4-5
│   ├── chat claude-opus-4-5 (CLIENT — one per real model call)
│   ├── execute_tool exec (INTERNAL — 156ms)
│   ├── execute_tool Read (INTERNAL — 12ms)
│   └── execute_tool web_fetch (INTERNAL — 1200ms)
├── openclaw.compaction (INTERNAL — if context is compacted)
└── openclaw.command.new (INTERNAL — if session reset)

All spans within a request share the same traceId and are linked via parent-child relationships.

docs.title: Request Span
docs.text:
Created by the message_received hook. This is the root span for the entire request lifecycle.

Field Value Span Name openclaw.request Kind SERVER

Attributes:

Attribute Type Description openclaw.message.channel string Source channel (whatsapp, telegram, discord, etc.) openclaw.session.key string Session identifier openclaw.message.direction string Always "inbound" openclaw.message.from string Sender identifier openclaw.request.duration_ms int Total request duration

docs.title: Agent Turn Span
docs.text:
Created by the before_model_resolve hook at the earliest point in the agent run, enriched by before_prompt_build once session history is loaded, and ended by agent_end. Child of the request span.

Prior to v0.2.0 this span was created in the legacy before_agent_start hook. See CHANGELOG and ISI-730 for the migration details.

Field Value Span Name openclaw.agent.turn Kind INTERNAL

Attributes:

Attribute Type Description openclaw.agent.id string Agent identifier openclaw.session.key string Session identifier openclaw.prompt.chars int Length of the user prompt (set by before_prompt_build) openclaw.session.message_count int Session history size fed to the LLM (set by before_prompt_build) openclaw.agent.duration_ms int Turn duration in milliseconds openclaw.agent.success boolean Whether the turn completed successfully openclaw.agent.error string Error message (if failed) gen_ai.usage.input_tokens int Total input tokens (including cache read/write) gen_ai.usage.output_tokens int Total output tokens gen_ai.response.model string Actual model used (from last assistant message) traceloop.span.kind string task — Traceloop/OpenLLMetry marker read by Dynatrace AI Observability gen_ai.input.messages string Opt-in. Input messages (JSON array, or flat prompt when no array). Gated by captureContent.inputMessages; redacted before truncation gen_ai.system_instructions string Opt-in. System-prompt text. Gated by captureContent.systemPrompt; redacted before truncation. Distinct from gen_ai.provider.name

Schema 1.4.0 (ISI-1605) added the opt-in GenAI content keys (gen_ai.input.messages, gen_ai.system_instructions, and on other spans gen_ai.output.messages, gen_ai.prompt.prompt_filter_results, gen_ai.completion.content_filter_results) plus the traceloop.span.kind marker. Content keys emit only when the matching captureContent flag is on (default off) and always pass through the redact-before-truncate funnel.

Schema 1.3.0 (ISI-1004) removed gen_ai.usage.total_tokens — compute it as gen_ai.usage.input_tokens + gen_ai.usage.output_tokens.

gen_ai.request.model on the turn span

The agent turn span no longer carries gen_ai.request.model — in OpenClaw 2026.2+ the model has not been resolved when the span is created (before_model_resolve fires pre-resolution). The resolved model is recorded as gen_ai.response.model at agent_end and is also available on openclaw.llm.call spans from the llm_input hook.

Token Counts

Token counts are summed across all assistant messages in the turn. If the agent makes multiple LLM calls (e.g., tool use loop), the totals reflect all calls combined. Cache tokens (cacheRead, cacheWrite) are included in the input token count.

docs.title: Tool Execution Spans
docs.text:
Created by the tool_result_persist hook. Child of the agent turn span.

Field Value Span Name execute_tool <tool_name> Kind INTERNAL

Examples: execute_tool exec, execute_tool web_fetch, execute_tool browser, execute_tool Read, execute_tool Write, execute_tool memory_search, execute_tool Edit

Attributes:

Attribute Type Description openclaw.tool.name string Tool name openclaw.tool.call_id string Unique tool call identifier openclaw.tool.is_synthetic boolean Whether the tool call is synthetic openclaw.tool.result_chars int Total characters in result openclaw.tool.result_parts int Number of content parts in result openclaw.tool.error_preview string Failure paths only. Bounded, redacted preview of the tool error text. Gated by captureContent.toolErrorMessages; redacted before truncation (1024 chars) openclaw.session.key string Session identifier openclaw.agent.id string Agent identifier gen_ai.tool.name string Tool name (GenAI semconv) gen_ai.operation.name string execute_tool traceloop.span.kind string tool — Traceloop/OpenLLMetry marker read by Dynatrace AI Observability

openclaw.tool.error_preview (ISI-1318) shipped in 0.7.0. It is written only when a tool call fails. Its captureContent.toolErrorMessages gate is the one content flag that defaults on when captureContent is supplied as an object — error text is operational data, a different privacy class from prompt/response bodies. See Configuration → captureContent.

Status: OK on success, ERROR if the tool returned an error.

docs.title: Outbound message span (openclaw.message.sent)
docs.text: When captureContent.outputMessages is enabled the outbound reply is also emitted as gen_ai.output.messages (alongside the legacy openclaw.content.output_message), redacted before truncation.

docs.title: Content-filter results (openclaw.llm.call / chat <model>)
docs.text: Azure/OpenAI content-filter payloads returned on the model response are emitted — when gated on — as gen_ai.prompt.prompt_filter_results (behind captureContent.inputMessages) and gen_ai.completion.content_filter_results (behind captureContent.outputMessages), JSON-encoded and redacted.

docs.title: Compaction Span
docs.text:
Created when the runtime compacts session context (a major context/token event). The span is opened by before_compaction and closed by after_compaction, and is nested under the active session/agent context so it appears inside the end-to-end trace rather than as a separate root.

Span Name openclaw.compaction Kind INTERNAL Attribute Type Description openclaw.compaction.reason string Why compaction ran (auto-compaction reports "auto") openclaw.compaction.messages_before int Session message count before compaction openclaw.compaction.messages_after int Session message count after compaction openclaw.compaction.tokens_before int Token count before compaction (when reported) openclaw.compaction.tokens_after int Token count after compaction (when reported) openclaw.compaction.tokens_reclaimed int tokens_before − tokens_after, clamped at 0 (when both known) openclaw.compaction.duration_ms int Compaction duration in milliseconds openclaw.session.key string Session identifier openclaw.agent.id string Agent identifier

Emits the openclaw.compaction.count counter and openclaw.compaction.tokens_reclaimed histogram (see the Metrics Reference).

docs.title: Command Spans
docs.text:
Created when session commands are issued.

Span Name Kind Description openclaw.command.new INTERNAL /new command openclaw.command.reset INTERNAL /reset command openclaw.command.stop INTERNAL /stop command

Attributes:

Attribute Type Description openclaw.command.action string Command name openclaw.command.session_key string Session identifier openclaw.command.source string Command source

docs.title: Gateway Spans
docs.text: Span Name Kind Description openclaw.gateway.startup INTERNAL Gateway startup event

docs.title: Trace Context Propagation
docs.text:
The plugin maintains a sessionContextMap keyed by sessionKey:

  1. message_received creates a root span and stores its context
  2. before_model_resolve creates an agent turn span as a child of the root
  3. before_prompt_build enriches the agent turn span with prompt/history attrs
  4. tool_result_persist creates tool spans as children of the agent turn
  5. agent_end ends the agent turn and root spans, cleans up the context

Stale contexts (no agent_end within 30 minutes) are automatically cleaned up (checked every 60s).

docs.title: Example DQL Queries (Dynatrace)
docs.text:
Token usage per agent turn:

fetch spans, samplingRatio:1
| filter contains(endpoint.name, "openclaw.agent.turn")
| fields start_time, duration, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens,
         gen_ai.usage.output_tokens,
         total_tokens = toLong(gen_ai.usage.input_tokens) + toLong(gen_ai.usage.output_tokens),
         gen_ai.response.model
| sort start_time desc
| limit 20

Tool execution breakdown:

fetch spans, samplingRatio:1
| filter startsWith(span.name, "execute_tool ")
| fields start_time, span.name, duration, openclaw.tool.result_chars
| sort start_time desc
| limit 50

Full trace for a session:

fetch spans, samplingRatio:1
| filter openclaw.session.key == "agent:main:main"
| fields start_time, span.name, duration, span.kind, trace.id
| sort start_time desc

Replace "agent:main:main" with your own session key — main here is just this example's agent id, not a fixed or implicit value. Your installation's agent id comes from agents.entries.<agentId> in openclaw.json, set at onboarding and renameable later; if you haven't renamed it from OpenClaw's setup-wizard default, it probably is main, but don't assume — check your config, or pull a real session key from a recent span instead of guessing.

docs.title: Semantic Conventions
docs.text: The plugin follows OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions for token-related attributes (gen_ai.usage.*, gen_ai.response.model). Custom OpenClaw attributes use the openclaw.* namespace.
